accepted.question_text: For the presheaf topos PSh(F), where F is the category of non-empty finite sets and all functions, determine in combinatorial or number-theoretic terms which pairs of levels l0 <= l1 satisfy the condition that every l0-skeletal object is l1-coskeletal. Equivalently, determine the Aufhebung relation for the topos of symmetric simplicial sets, that is, the quantitative relation between recovering structures from small quotient structures and recovering them from small substructures.

evidence.quote: Given two levels l1 >= l0 of a topos E, we say that l1 is way above l0 if every l0-skeletal object is l1-coskeletal.

[Law09] [...] There is another fundamental topos related to classical constructions and combinatorial topology, namely the Boolean algebra classifier that consists of presheaves on the category of finite non-empty sets. [...] What is, in combinatorial or number-theoretic terms, the way below relation for this basic topos?
This result provides a solution to the fourth of the seven open problems in topos theory posed by Lawvere in 2009.

accepted.question_text: Fix an integer n > 2. Define Phi_G on subsets S of the vertex set V of an undirected graph G = (V, E) by Phi_G(S) = S union {v in V | there exist distinct s0, s1 in S with {s0, v} and {s1, v} both edges of G}. A graph is propagative if for every two-element subset S of V there exists k >= 1 such that Phi_G^k(S) = V. Determine the smallest integer m such that every undirected graph with n vertices and minimum degree at least m is necessarily propagative.

evidence.quote: We call G propagative if, for any S subset V with |S| = 2, there exists k >= 1 such that Phi^k S = V.
Puzzle 3.1.2. Fix n > 2. Find the minimum m such that any undirected graph G = (V, E) with - |V| = n, and - each v in V has degree at least m is necessarily propagative.
This bound is in fact sharp; that is, the answer to Puzzle 3.1.2 is m = floor(n/2) + 1.
